text:
maya: Heads-up: after landing the prefill-aware packing tweak on canary, we're seeing a p50 token latency bump on small-chat workloads. Not huge but noticeable.
sam: saw that in dashboard. p50 went from ~42ms -> ~68ms for 1-2k token budgets. p90 is stable. interesting.
liam: any kernel selection flips in the trace? that usually explains a 1.5-2x step.
maya: I pulled one trace. kernel changed from fused-attn-v2 to generic-attn when batch shape changed (more small-seq, high-prefix-hit). snippet:
```
batch_shape: [4, 512] -> [8, 128]
kernel: fused-attn-v2 (fast) -> generic-attn (fallback)
kv_cache_hit_ratio: 0.62
continuous_batch_budget: 1024 -> 512 per-microbatch
```
nora: hmm that microbatch split looks like the packer is prioritizing fill count over token continuity. Prefill hits increase, so effective sequence length drops -> different kernel chosen.
sam: profiling confirms. when avg_seq_len < 200 and num_seqs > 6 we pick generic-attn because our kernel selector currently thresholds on seq_len * num_heads heuristics. here's profiler excerpt (wall):
```
fused-attn-v2: 0.8ms/token
generic-attn: 1.6ms/token
cost delta ~2x for short tokens
```
maya: the packing change improves throughput CPU-side but incurs per-token kernel overhead. net effect bad for latency SLOs on small-chat.
liam: two options:
- adjust batcher policy to cap microbatch width (prefer longer sequences) when prefix-hit ratio > X
- tweak kernel selector to consider kv_cache_hit_ratio and choose fused-attn for high-hit cases even at lower seq_len
nora: also consider raising token budget target for continuous batching under prefill-heavy workloads. right now we set budget=1024 which gets chopped into small microbatches when many hits exist.
sam: agree. quick experiment: set continuous_batch_budget=1536 and soft_min_seq=256 for 2 hours on canary.
maya: will try. deploying patch now. @deploy-bot canary deploy details?
deploy-bot: deployment started: canary/pack-prefill-20240210 -> 6 hosts. health checks running.
liam: also add a fallback rule: if kernel selector would pick generic-attn but kv_cache_hit_ratio > 0.5 AND avg_seq_len_after_pack > 120, force fused-attn. cheap guard.
maya: implemented selector override locally. re-ran perf tests: p50 back to ~46ms. p90 unchanged. looks promising.
sam: nice. can we add a metric: kernel_mismatch_rate (pack predicted kernel != chosen kernel) to alert on these regressions?
nora: yes, and tag it with prefix_hit_bucket so we can correlate.
maya: logging added to canary. i'll keep monitors for 4h and then roll to prod if stable. open question: does this change affect throughput on long-form workloads?
liam: unlikely; override only triggers when kv_hit_ratio > 0.5 and avg_seq_len_after_pack < 300. long-form unaffected.
sam: please add a short note in the PR about selector heuristics and this behavioral regression so we don't regress again.
maya: will do. thanks all.
liam: one more: put a small experiment in A/B to test token budget=1536 vs 1024 across different traffic shapes.
maya: adding AB test config in runtime flags.
sam: great. if this stabilizes, we should update docs on packer heuristics and kernel selector interplay.
maya: agreed. end-of-thread summary: cause = packer prefill strategy reduced seq lengths -> kernel flip -> latency regression. mitigation = selector override + raise batch token budget + AB test. will report results.
